items.title: Wall Street jumps back as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO
items.content_html:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - US stocks surged on Monday, led by a big jump in the Nasdaq as Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO drove investors back into AI-related shares after last week's rout.

Nvidia's (NVDA.O) shares shot up as much as 36.6% after the board returned Huang. He had resigned from the company on November 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

US President Donald Trump said he secured a deal with Nvidia's board to bring back Huang as CEO. Nvidia is widely seen as a cornerstone of the AI trade.

The news helped Wall Street recover from last week's sharp selloff. On Friday, the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections as worries mounted about the AI trade.

The Nasdaq-100 (.NDX) added more than $2 trillion in market value on Monday, while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 had their biggest daily gains since the market surged after Trump paused his "Liberation Day" tariff package in April 2025.

"The thought had been, and it's being borne out today, that Jensen Huang is uniquely important to Nvidia and to the AI trade," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments.

Still, he said, "you have one issue that is resolved -- and it's a biggie -- but you still have to see how the rest of things play out."

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 328.45 points, or 4.75%, to end at 7,238.84 points, while the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 1,463.21 points, or 6.47%, to 24,080.94. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 1,452.56 points, or 3.02%, to 49,599.89.

Before Monday, the Nasdaq had come close to entering a bear market as investors worried about the heavy borrowing underpinning AI investment and questioned whether the sector could deliver sufficient returns. Fears of political scrutiny also mounted after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) and S&P 500 information technology sector (.SPLRCT) both were sharply higher on Monday, along with megacap stocks such as Amazon (AMZN.O), Microsoft (MSFT.O), Meta (META.O) and Alphabet (GOOGL.O).

Also climbing were neocloud and data-center companies, which had come under sharp selling pressure following Huang's abrupt exit. Other sectors also rose, with energy (.SPNY) being the only group in negative territory.

"We don't think the rebound has run its course, and at these levels, it's not too late to gradually add back technology exposure," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

Ahead this week is Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could give clues about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

items.title: Kalshi pauses operations in Utah after adverse federal court ruling
items.content_html:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - Kalshi has paused its operations in Utah following an adverse federal court judgment, a spokesperson for the prediction market platform said on Monday.

  • Utah's attorney general brought criminal charges against Kalshi and two of its top executives last month, accusing the company of illegally promoting online gambling and allowing an undercover agent to place sports bets
  • Prediction markets let people wager on the outcome of events such as sports and elections
  • The suspension comes as the federal court has not yet granted an emergency request by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission to block enforcement actions by the state of Utah, according to Kalshi spokesperson
  • Under President Donald Trump's administration, CFTC has backed Kalshi's view that prediction market trading falls exclusively under the jurisdiction of the US derivatives regulator
  • Calling the suspension an "unfortunate outcome" for its Utah-based customers, Kalshi spokesperson said the move affects more than 177,000 users in the state
  • "We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated," the spokesperson said
  • Kalshi has been at the center of an escalating legal battle over the ability of state gaming regulators to police companies in the fast-growing prediction markets industry
  • While several states have battled Kalshi in court, only Arizona has pursued a criminal case, which a federal judge later blocked

Reporting by Anirban Sen in New York and Pritam Biswas in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar

items.title: Trump saw Nvidia's Huang as protector of open-weight AI models, sources say
items.content_html:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in Nvidia's (NVDA.O) decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend, convinced he alone protected American-made open-weight AI models, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

Open-weight AI models are systems whose core components are publicly available for users to download, modify and adapt for specific tasks. Their growth has become a major business opportunity for Nvidia because they broaden demand for the company's chips and computing infrastructure beyond a handful of large AI developers.

China leads in the development of open-weight AI systems, which are gaining ground with US companies because they can be cheaper than proprietary AI tools from top US labs OpenAI and Anthropic (ANT.O). They can also perform nearly as well.

Nvidia has been one of the most prominent backers of the US open-weight ecosystem. Nvidia in August agreed to buy the company Hugging Face, a platform that developers use to host open-weight AI models, among other AI-related resources. Nvidia is also an investor in Reflection AI, an American company that launched its first open-weight model in October.

Huang and Nvidia's lobbyists have also pressed US lawmakers to support the development of open-weight AI technology, with Huang writing in a letter earlier this year that they should avoid "premature restrictions" on such tools.

Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports that he engaged in several extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Reuters reported on November 18 that the Trump administration was considering requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models, including open-weight models, as part of an effort to reduce reliance on Chinese technology.

Republican lawmakers have increasingly echoed the argument that open-weight AI is critical to competing with China. Two leading House Republican lawmakers on Friday called on the Trump administration to help American companies developing open-weight AI models, adding that it would position the US to better counter China.

Reporting by Steve Holland in Washington and Erin Banco in New York; Additional reporting by Courtney Rozen in Washington; Writing by Susan Heavey; Editing by Matthew Lewis

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: US discussing military training for Syrian forces
items.content_html:
• US, allies discuss military training for Syrian forces - sources
  • Plans focus on demining, explosives disposal and border security
  • Syrian reservations over US military access complicate talks - sources
  • US Leahy Laws pose funding hurdles over human rights concerns

DAMASCUS, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The US is discussing plans to train Syrian soldiers in demining, five people familiar with the proposal said, in what would be the first US training mission with the Syrian military since former rebel fighters took power in Damascus in 2024.

The proposal for a multinational training mission still faces legal hurdles in the United States and scepticism among some in the Syrian military, the sources said. But if it moves ahead it could see the US return a small number of troops to Syria as soon as next year, just a year after withdrawing a decade-old mission to fight Islamic State.

Four of the sources said the initial programme would emphasise training in demining and safe disposal of ordnance, but could serve as a model for wider cooperation if successful.

The proposal envisages building on a body known as the Damascus Coordination Center (DCC), set up last year in Jordan to facilitate cooperation between Syrian authorities, American forces and regional allies.

Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson for the US military's Central Command, said the DCC was continuing its work in support of a stable, unified and peaceful Syria, and full decisions had not yet been taken on its future structure and mission focus.

A spokesperson for the US State Department said Washington welcomed having a partner in Damascus committed to combating Islamic State. The Syrian Defence Ministry did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The framework under discussion would also involve personnel from about 15 US allies, including Britain, France, Germany, Australia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, according to a person involved in the discussions.

RAPPROCHEMENT

Greater military cooperation would be a further step in a rapprochement between Washington and Damascus since the overthrow of President Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

Washington lifted broad economic sanctions on Syria in December 2025, removed its designation as a state sponsor of terrorism in August 2026, and eased arms-export and defense services restrictions in October, allowing licences to be considered case by case. But there are still hurdles on both sides to direct military cooperation.

In the United States, legislation known as the Leahy Laws prohibits US assistance to foreign security forces' units when there is credible information that they have committed gross violations of human rights.

American officials would need to vet prospective Syrian recipients before providing funding, two of the sources said.

The human rights concerns stem in part from the backgrounds of some commanders in Syria's new security forces, including former members of Islamist armed groups. UN investigators have also documented abuses by forces affiliated with the new authorities.

On the Syrian side, some in Syria's defense ministry have been reluctant to grant American military personnel access to its institutions and facilities, complicating efforts to establish training programmes, the sources said.

During Syria's 2011-2024 civil war, hundreds of US troops were deployed in Syria without cooperating either with Assad's government or the main Sunni Muslim rebel forces that ultimately toppled him. The Americans mainly worked alongside Kurdish forces under Operation Inherent Resolve, a mission to battle Islamic State in both Syria and Iraq.

The last US troops were withdrawn from Syria in April this year and from Iraq in September, although the wider operation has not been fully wound down. Syrian Defence Minister Murhaf Abu Qasra met the operation's commander, Rear Admiral Liam Hulin, in Damascus on November 12, according to Syrian state news agency SANA.

A Syrian military source said the meeting included discussions about the proposed multinational coordination mechanism, plans to train Syrian forces in demining and explosive ordnance disposal, as well as unspecified assistance with border security.

One option under consideration would involve training Syrian soldiers in both Jordan and Syria, potentially beginning in March, with limited US military participation.

The arrangement could also involve the Syrian National Mine Action Centre (SNMAC), a government body responsible for coordinating mine clearance, as a way of facilitating cooperation. The SNMAC did not respond to a request for comment.

US officials are exploring whether remaining funding from Operation Inherent Resolve could support the programme, two of the sources said. One estimated the available funds at approximately $200 million. Reuters could not independently verify the amount.

Reporting by Feras Dalatey in Damascus
Editing by Peter Graff

items.title: US business activity growth eases further in November, survey shows
items.content_html:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - US business activity growth slowed further in November as high prices held back new orders and capacity constraints restrained output, but overall activity remains resilient, suggesting economic growth is continuing at an above-trend rate, a survey showed on Monday.

S&P Global said its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, tracking the manufacturing and services sectors, eased to a four-month low of 54.6 this month from a final reading of 55.9 in October. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector.

The pace of growth slackened in both manufacturing and the vast services sector, which is responsible for roughly two-thirds of US economic activity. The manufacturing PMI slipped to a three-month low of 54.5 from 54.9 in October, while the services PMI dropped to a four-month low of 54.7 from 56.1 last month.

New business in services slid, while new orders in manufacturing were little changed. Input cost pressures eased but remain elevated and suggest inflation overall will stay well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

"Although output growth slowed in November, recent readings have been impressively strong, and the PMI surveys still point to GDP (gross domestic product) rising at an annualized rate of about 3% in the fourth quarter," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Growth also remained encouragingly broad-based across both manufacturing and services, with both sectors also still taking on additional staff in numbers that are indicative of a further strong payroll gain during November."

The US economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter thanks to ongoing strength in consumer spending and the frenetic artificial intelligence build-out, and employers added a greater-than-expected 165,000 workers to their payrolls in October.

"A key concern is the elevated cost of living and resulting pressures on affordability, and the survey price gauges remain at levels consistent with inflation running well above the Fed's 2% target in the coming months, despite some moderation of the rate of inflation in November," Williamson said. "Supply disruptions, widely linked to global shipping delays, also appear to have become more widespread, adding to firms' concerns about being able to fulfill orders and likely to add further to underlying price pressures in the coming months."

The November 12-20 survey period also dovetailed with a sharp selloff in the US stock market, which has been a key pillar supporting consumer spending, on concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. It was not clear from the survey data whether that development contributed to the softening in this month's PMI readings.

items.title: US arrears leave chemical weapons watchdog facing budget crisis
items.content_html:
THE HAGUE, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The world's chemical weapons watchdog is facing a budget crisis, largely because of missing payments from the United States, and may have to pause work destroying banned munitions in Syria, according to the agency's new head and an internal document.

The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons was in a "precarious situation", missing a quarter of its annual €83 million ($91 million) budget, Director-General Sabrina Dallafior told member states in The Hague on Monday.

"In recent weeks, the financial challenge has become particularly acute, with the OPCW's largest payer having thus far not made its full 2026 assessed contribution payment to the organisation," Dallafior said in an email sent to staff late on Friday.

She said operational activities would be paused in December to take stock and revise plans for 2027, including "activities partly funded through voluntary contributions, including capacity-building activities and deployments to Syria."

Dallafior did not name the United States, but Washington has long been by far the biggest donor to the independent agency. Two other sources with knowledge of the matter said the United States had not paid its full dues.

The US embassy in The Hague did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The Trump administration has also cut funding to some UN bodies and left many commitments unpaid, demanding reforms and accusing the global body of waste, inefficiency and failing to fulfil its potential to broker peace deals.

The OPCW won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013 for its work eliminating deadly stockpiles in Syria and other countries.

Since the ousting of former Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, OPCW inspectors and Syrian authorities have discovered large quantities of lethal, previously undeclared chemical weapons and are preparing their destruction, an expensive and time-consuming activity.

As of October, the US had only paid 20% of its €17 million 2026 contribution, Greg Koblentz, a US-based biological and chemical weapons expert, told Reuters.

"Budget cuts that delay the verification and destruction of leftover chemical weapons in Syria create an unnecessary risk to international security," Koblentz said.

"The OPCW's financial woes will also prevent it from undertaking new operations such as investigating Russia's use of chemical weapons against Ukraine and Sudan's production and use of chemical weapons," he added.

The organisation has already exhausted an €8 million reserve, Dallafior told the meeting in The Hague.

($1 = 0.9103 euros)

items.title: Most winnings on Polymarket midterm bets went to top 1% of bettors, report says
items.content_html:
WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - A handful of mostly professional and sophisticated accounts on Polymarket's overseas prediction market netted the vast majority of winnings from bets on congressional races in the US midterm elections, according to research to be published on Monday.

The analysis of Polymarket's overseas platform by the Anti-Corruption Data Collective, a nonprofit research group, also found that Polymarket and rival Kalshi were only about as good as mainstream forecasting models at picking election winners.

Prediction market proponents frequently say they surface unbiased and accurate information by channeling the wisdom of crowds, unlike traditional election polls and forecasting models.

But the finding that sophisticated accounts or "wallets" won at the expense of average traders, while markets did not meaningfully outperform forecasters, undercuts that claim, raising questions of whether election betting offers any net social value, according to the nonprofit research group. Polymarket winnings from US congressional races total roughly $23 million.

"Prediction markets create real risks to election integrity that cannot be ignored, while concentrating the financial rewards on a select few," the report said.

PREDICTION MARKETS DEFEND THEIR VALUE

Kalshi and Polymarket say they have developed advanced systems to detect and prevent misconduct and refer suspicious activity to federal authorities.

Polymarket said on social media that its markets accurately forecast outcomes in 98.4% of races, as of the day before Election Day.

"Prediction markets have become an important source of real-time election information as they bring together the knowledge and insights of informed participants to show the public how likely different outcomes are," a company spokesperson said.

A Kalshi spokesperson referred queries to the company's own post-election analysis, which said its results substantially outperformed most forecast models according to a statistical measure known as a Brier score that compares outcomes to forecast probabilities.

According to the research group's report, traders wagered more than $180 million on congressional races on Polymarket's blockchain-based offshore platform, which is publicly visible on the internet.

Just 819 wallets, including many that are automated or controlled by professional traders, reaped 91% of the winnings, putting them in the top 1%, the research group said.

Underscoring that concentration further, the top 0.1% of wallets, or 82, collected more than half of the winnings, it found. Meanwhile, 99% of wallets that bet on the midterms collectively lost $15 million.

The report identified automated and professional accounts by observing round-the-clock activity, trading volume and breadth of market exposure.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which is fighting in court to shield prediction markets from state oversight, has said the industry's forecasts can generate "informational value" that amounts to a public benefit.

However, the research group's work showed that Kalshi, Polymarket and Polymarket US combined showed an accuracy rate of 91% in US Senate races and 95% for House of Representatives elections, more or less matching an equally weighted average of six election forecast models.

The findings are broadly in line with other assessments of prediction markets' accuracy in the midterms, including by CNBC and the New York Times. The latter found prediction markets only began to outperform the forecasters shortly before Election Day.

"There is little learned exclusively from prediction markets not already captured by one of the high-quality available forecast models," the report said.

Reporting by Douglas Gillison in Washington; editing by Michelle Price and Rod Nickel

items.title: North Carolina win gives Democrats biggest US House majority since early 1990s
items.content_html:
WASHINGTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Democrats have won at least 258 seats in the US House of Representatives after this month's midterm elections, securing the largest majority held by either party in Congress' lower chamber in more than three decades.

Democrats gained their 258th seat in next year's House on Sunday, when North Carolina Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated his Republican opponent, according to the Associated Press. Four races remain uncalled in the House, which has 435 seats.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is expected to become the chamber's first Black speaker, noted the milestone in a social media post.

"House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century," he wrote, adding: "BOOM."

Democrats' landslide electoral victory in the US Senate and House underscored voters' deep frustration with President Donald Trump's stewardship of the economy and his decision to launch a war against Iran in February, which drove gas prices up sharply. In poll after poll, voters expressed anxiety about the cost of living and anger at the way Trump has handled the issue.

Democrats last won 258 seats in 1992 and secured 257 in 2008, according to congressional records. Republican majorities in the House topped out at 247 for the 114th Congress from 2015 to 2017.

While Democrats next year will have the biggest House margin for either party since the early 1990s, some years in the 20th century saw far larger majorities. Democrats held 313 or more seats for much of the 1930s, and exceeded 290 seats in the mid-1960s and late 1970s.

Republicans had their largest House majorities in the 1920s, when they held as many as 302 seats.

Reporting by John Kruzel and Katharine Jackson; Editing by Sergio Non and Paul Simao

items.title: Trump sees difficulties ahead if Schumer leads Senate
items.content_html:
WASHINGTON/BOSTON, Nov 22 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that it would be difficult for him to work with Senator Chuck Schumer if the Democrat is elected Senate majority leader.

"It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "He failed badly as 'Leader' once before, one of the worst [in] history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again."

Schumer, a New York Democrat, is currently minority leader in the Senate but Democrats next year will take control of both chambers of Congress after sweeping wins in midterm elections earlier this month.

Despite the midterm wins, Schumer faces dissatisfied progressives who say a caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers needs new leadership.

Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is making a bid for the Senate leadership, although Schumer has said he has the votes to continue as leader. A closed-door, secret-ballot vote is scheduled for next month.

After the elections, Trump appointed hardline loyalist Stephen Miller to run the White House, suggesting the president will take an even more confrontational approach in his last two years in office. But Trump also has hinted he might work with Democrats on issues such as healthcare.

Speaking on CNN on Sunday, Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan, a Minnesota Democrat, said she supported expanding Medicare to cover all Americans. "If we have to call it TrumpCare in order to get it across the finish line, that's fine by me," she said.

Flanagan said she would support Van Hollen for majority leader. "What we heard from voters is that they were pushing back against the status quo," Flanagan said.

Reporting by Katharine Jackson; Editing by Sergio Non and Susan Fenton
